question.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{e}^{5x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{5x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{e}^{5x}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We, substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{5x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{{e}^{5x}}{5}-\int \frac{{e}^{5x}}{5}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{5x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{x{e}^{5x}}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\int {e}^{5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{5x}}{5}-\frac{{e}^{5x}}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$
